# Cohort 104: shared native startup actor construction

Approved #2542/#2151 original selected construction/raw_sql_policy and generation
write-fence ownership govern. Two shared actual-runtime helpers now consume native
PostgreSQL construction rather than exposing a pool and constructing a wrapper:
assertNativeRuntimeStartCarriesMemoryIdentity and proveRuntimeConstructedActorCensusBothStores.
SQLite already consumes its original native owner. No new helper/domain owner is added.

The former serves direct and nested filesystem flow memory-identity journeys; the
latter serves restart, source-set rebind, retained refresh/terminal drain, atomic
rebind retry and partial refresh/shutdown. Their source compilation, exact source/run
setup, explicit runtime dependencies, process occurrence and generation admission,
actual startup, flow construction, attachment, configured memory, restart/rebind
assertions and joined cleanup remain byte-for-byte except the constructor replacement.
Native fixture close is registered before their runtime/process/capability cleanup.

Two finite full-helper recipes/type overlay cover all seven roots. The oracle permits
only the exact PostgreSQL construction substitutions and rejects foreign backend/test
or reconstructed admission. Focused both-store race proof covers direct/nested memory
and constructed actor restart. Other rebind/refresh paths retain their full exact recipe
and already share the corrected constructor; their remaining raw readiness observations
and trigger faults remain explicitly tracked debt, not claimed canonicalized here.

Value: shared runtime/admission setup and resource ownership rather than an isolated
read migration; no measured flake-rate claim. No production semantics/spec change,
compatibility/framework/architecture split or new issue. Parent closure remains open.
